text: All green. Committing the retry fix as the first focused commit (three files), and running vet across the repo in parallel since it doesn't depend on the commit.

command:
git add pipedrive/raw.go pipedrive/raw_test.go pipedrive/v1/files_test.go && git -c user.name="Claude Fable 5.1" -c user.email="noreply@anthropic.com" commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(raw): buffer non-replayable request bodies so uploads retry

Raw.Do handed io.Reader bodies straight to http.NewRequest, which only
derives GetBody for *bytes.Buffer, *bytes.Reader and *strings.Reader.
An *os.File or any wrapped reader therefore left GetBody nil, the retry
transport treated the request as non-replayable, and Files.Add,
Files.Update and Persons.AddPicture returned the first 429/5xx to the
caller regardless of RetryPolicy. The body was also sent chunked.

Such readers are now drained into memory once before the request is
built, so every attempt sends identical bytes with an explicit
Content-Length. Readers that implement io.Closer are closed after
draining, matching net/http's handling of request bodies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git status --short
go vet ./... 2>&1 | grep -v "stat cache" | tail -5; echo "vet exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

text: Commit 1 is in place and vet is clean. Next, the ergonomic upload API. Writing the `Files.Upload` tests and its implementation together, since they touch different files.

command:
perl -0pi -e 's/## \[Unreleased\]
/## [Unreleased]

### Added

- `v1.Files.Upload` uploads a file from a file name and an `io.Reader`, building
  the `multipart/form-data` body internally the way `CallLogs.AddRecording`
  does. `WithUploadFileDealID`, `WithUploadFilePersonID`,
  `WithUploadFileOrganizationID`, `WithUploadFileProductID`,
  `WithUploadFileActivityID`, `WithUploadFileLeadID` and
  `WithUploadFileProjectID` associate the file with a record and are validated
  client-side; `WithFilesQuery` and `WithFilesRequestOptions` are accepted as
  well. The encoded body is replayable, so uploads retry under the configured
  `RetryPolicy`.

### Fixed

- Uploads through `v1.Files.Add`, `v1.Files.Update` and `v1.Persons.AddPicture`
  returned the first 429/502/503/504 to the caller instead of retrying, whatever
  the `RetryPolicy`, whenever the body was not a `*bytes.Reader`,
  `*bytes.Buffer` or `*strings.Reader` (for example an `*os.File`). `net/http`
  cannot replay such readers, so the retry transport gave up. `RawClient.Do` now
  buffers these bodies before sending, giving every attempt identical bytes and
  an explicit `Content-Length` instead of a chunked upload. Readers that
  implement `io.Closer` are closed once drained, as `net/http` already did.
/' CHANGELOG.md && sed -n 8,34p CHANGELOG.md
sed -n 14,107p README.md

perl -0pi -e 's/## Retries and per-request options
/## File uploads (API v1)

File storage is a v1-only endpoint. `client.Files.Upload` takes a file name
and an `io.Reader`, encodes the `multipart/form-data` body for you and attaches
the file to a record:

```go
client, err := v1.NewClient(pipedrive.Config{
	Auth: pipedrive.APITokenAuth("YOUR_API_TOKEN"),
})
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}

f, err := os.Open("contract.pdf")
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
defer f.Close()

file, err := client.Files.Upload(
	context.Background(),
	filepath.Base(f.Name()),
	f,
	v1.WithUploadFileDealID(v1.DealID(123)),
)
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
log.Printf("file id=%d", file.ID)
```

The encoded body is buffered in memory, so a 429 or 5xx response is retried
under the configured `RetryPolicy`. `Files.Add` remains available when you
already have a body and content type; a body that `net/http` cannot replay,
such as an `*os.File`, is buffered the same way before it is sent.

## Retries and per-request options
/' README.md && grep -n "^## " README.md

feat(v1): add Files.Upload with built-in multipart encoding

Files.Add required callers to assemble the multipart/form-data body and
content type themselves, unlike CallLogs.AddRecording which takes a file

Both parts of the report are addressed, on branch `fix/files-upload-retry` in three local commits. Nothing is pushed.

**Root cause of the retry failure.** `Files.Add` passed the caller's reader straight to the standard library request constructor. Go only derives a replayable body for byte buffers, byte readers and string readers. An open file left `GetBody` nil, so the retry transport treated the request as non-replayable and returned the first 429 unchanged. The `RetryAllMethods` flag never came into play, and the upload also went out chunked with no content length. The same defect affected `Files.Update` and `Persons.AddPicture`.

**What changed**

- **Raw client buffers non-replayable bodies.** In `pipedrive/raw.go`, any reader the standard library cannot replay is drained into memory once before the request is built. Every retry attempt sends identical bytes with an explicit content length. Readers that implement `io.Closer` are closed after draining, which preserves the previous ownership behaviour. The retry transport itself is unchanged, matching how the SDK already handled multipart bodies.
- **New `Files.Upload`.** It takes a file name and an `io.Reader`, mirroring `CallLogs.AddRecording`, and builds the multipart body internally. Association options cover deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead and project IDs, validated client-side. Existing `WithFilesQuery` and `WithFilesRequestOptions` values are accepted too. The old `Add` signature is untouched and now delegates to a shared helper.
- **Multipart helper accepts plain fields.** `internal/multipartbody` writes extra form fields ahead of the file part so association IDs travel in the same replayable body.
